text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello, I'm Holly. Can you hear me alright?
B: Hiya, yeah, loud and clear! I'm Gemma. How's your day going?
A: Honestly good, this is my third one and I'm sort of loving it. I'm just chatting to strangers all afternoon and calling it research. Where are you?
B: Warrington. North West, between Manchester and Liverpool. And you?
A: Birmingham, Kings Heath. But I grew up in Stafford, so I'm sort of Midlands-Midlands.
B: Oh, I know Stafford! Well, I've driven past it on the M6, sorry, that's not the same thing, is it?
A: Ha, that's how most people know it, to be fair. Is that a Lab in your photo? The black tail?
B: That's Bonnie. She's lovely but she's daft. She ate a whole sock last month and we ended up at the emergency vet on a Sunday night. Cost us a fortune.
A: A whole sock! Stop it. I've got a greyhound, Pickle, and she's the opposite, she won't eat anything unless it's warmed up. She's a proper diva. And I was literally just talking to a vet nurse, and apparently greyhounds are dead sensitive to anaesthetic, so now I'm worried about her teeth.
B: Oh no, bless her. Has she got to go in?
A: Next month, a dental. I'll be fine. Well, I won't, I'll be a wreck, but she'll be fine. What do you do, Gemma?
B: I'm office and accounts admin for a scaffolding company. Purchase ledger, timesheets, booking jobs in. I'm the one who knows where everything is, if that makes sense.
A: Oh, every office needs one of you, and they all fall apart without you. You actually reminded me a bit of my mum when I saw your photo, she's very much a calendar person. Is that your calendar in the background with all the writing?
B: Ha, that's me, yeah. Colour-coded. I'm not apologising for it. Netball's in green, church is in blue, Craig's jobs in red. Craig's my husband, he's an electrician, so his stuff moves around all the time and it drives me mad.
A: I need that. I'm a PhD student and my whole life is in my head and on about nine sticky notes. I've got a conference in three weeks and I haven't written the paper, so, you know.
B: Oh, three weeks! I'd be up at night. What's the PhD about?
A: Old canal-side industrial sites, warehouses and that, and how people sort of reclaim them. Raves, fishing, graffiti, people having a can by the water. You've got canals up your way, haven't you?
B: We've got the Sankey Canal, yeah, I walk Bonnie along there. There's all sorts of old bits of locks and walls. I never thought of it as anything really. It's just where you go with the dog.
A: That is literally my whole thesis! "It's just where you go with the dog." Can I quote you on that?
B: Ha, go on then, if it helps. I don't really know much about geography, to be honest.
A: Neither do I half the time. Okay, quick one, important. A bread roll. What do you call it?
B: A barm. Every time. I had a lady from Wales earlier and she'd never heard of it!
A: Ceri? Oh, I had her first round, she's brilliant. I say bap. It's a Stafford thing. My nan does a Sunday dinner and there's always a bap on the side for no reason, even with Yorkshires.
B: Bread with a roast? Oh, I'm not sure about that. We do tea on a Sunday at my mum's, and it's a proper roast, but
